title: findings@4
description: Successor to findings@1, the CLUSTER document — the one declared on the `aggregate` step whose declared severity order the ordered thresholds compile from. Identical to findings@1 in every constraint (`id` stays optional for the V30 reason findings@1 records; `severity` stays scalar-or-array as the aggregate's input contract), plus the optional `prior_disposition` from the retro of 2026-08-19. That retro measured what an undeclared disposition costs: RUN-29's round 1 restated 9 of 19 clusters near-verbatim from round 0's deferred items (3 titles byte-identical), and one locus the operator had already accepted at round 0 with a tracked follow-up came back as a fresh high at round 1 and was HELD again at round 2, spending a second operator ruling on settled ground. A cluster carrying `prior_disposition` is recognisable as a re-occurrence rather than a discovery. The field is OPTIONAL and additive: a payload that never sets it validates exactly as it did against findings@1, and `additionalProperties` stays true so the conjunction with `aggregate@1` remains satisfiable (V30).

id.description: Stable identifier for the finding or cluster, unique within the payload. Not `required`: the builtin `aggregate` carries through only the input element's own keys, so a schema requiring `id` makes the §7.6 E5 conjunction unsatisfiable and V30 refuses the workflow at register time.

severity.description: The finding's severity, on 02 §6's five-value ladder. The enum's document order IS the order thresholds compare on (`any(severity >= high)`) and the order `aggregate` reduces over: info < low < medium < high < blocker. Judges author on the general or security ladder fragment and map onto these values at emit time.

file.description: Repo-relative path the finding is anchored to.

evidence.description: What a skeptic can re-run or re-read to confirm the finding.

alternative.description: A concrete alternative to the flagged approach. OPTIONAL at every severity: the judge-design rule pairing a blocker with an alternative is a prose obligation in that contract, and synthesize-findings — which emits this same payload and adds no alternative — would be refused by a schema-level conditional (DKT-51).

members.description: The cluster's member severities, in arrival order. Present on the `aggregate` output ONLY. It is NOT how synthesize-findings carries a cluster: the builtin's `clusterMembers` reads member severities from the `severity` field of each input element, so 06 §2's scalar-or-array shape is the aggregate's INPUT contract — a multi-member cluster arrives with `severity` itself holding the array. That is also why synthesize's step declares no `payload`: this document's property-level `enum` on `severity` would refuse every multi-member cluster at `complete`. Values are the same ladder as `severity`; the constraint is not repeated as an `enum` here because `aggregate@1` leaves `members` unconstrained and the conjunction of the two documents must stay satisfiable (V30).

held.description: Set by the builtin `aggregate` (06 §2): the cluster's spread reached `hold_spread`, so it is excluded from automatic routing and materializes a `<step>-held` human step.

demoted_from.description: Set by `aggregate` when the computed value sits below the cluster's maximum member — the recorded demotion trail (02 §6). Absent when nothing was demoted. Under `method = "max"` this is structurally absent; it stays declared because other workflows still aggregate by median.

operator_resolved.description: Set when an operator accepted a held cluster's value via `docket step approve|reject`; thresholds re-apply over the resolved set (02 §6). It records that THIS round's hold was decided, and does not survive into a later round — `prior_disposition` is what carries a decision forward.

prior_disposition.description: How this same locus was already ruled on in an EARLIER fix-loop round. Set by synthesize-findings when its inputs identify a cluster as a re-occurrence, and carried through unchanged by `aggregate`. Its presence is the signal that the cluster is settled ground rather than a discovery: a reader — human or panel — owes it a re-read of the earlier ruling before spending a second decision. Absent on a genuinely new cluster, which is the ordinary case. Every sub-field is optional so a partially-known disposition is still recordable; an empty object records nothing and is no better than omitting the field. A re-review round's payload spans the STANDING SET, not the delta: a finding still open is carried forward with this key set even when it did not re-occur in that round's inputs, emitted as one element carrying the scalar the previous aggregate reduced it to rather than its original member array — spread 0, so `hold_spread` cannot re-hold ground an operator already ruled on. Clustering only the delta dropped 24 open findings, nine of them high, out of every later aggregate in RUN-31.

round.description: The fix-loop round the ruling was made in, 0-based — round 0 is the first review, before any fix step ran.

ruling.description: What was decided, in the decider's terms. Conventional forms: `accepted` (the computed value stood), `corrected-to-<severity>` (approved with `--value`), `rejected`, or `deferred` (accepted on the promise of later work, which `follow_up_issue` must then name).

ruled_by.description: Who decided: `operator`, or `panel <proposal-id>` where a tribunal did. A ruling with no name is not a ruling anyone can re-read.

follow_up_issue.description: The issue id the deferred work was filed as. REQUIRED IN PRACTICE when `ruling` is a deferral: a deferral with no issue is the evaporation this field exists to make visible (RUN-19: two approved hold remedies, no next round, no issue anywhere in the store). Not schema-required, because a schema-level conditional here would refuse payloads the aggregate legitimately carries through.
